Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Expectation2: Recite and reflect on the Quran
Situation2: A relaxed evening lies ahead with no other commitments.
Story: I finally settled onto my bed, the house quiet, the evening stretching ahead with no obligations. I had been looking forward to this moment all day—a chance to recite and reflect on the Quran, something I’d been neglecting lately. Just as I opened the mushaf, my phone buzzed. It was a message from Sarah: “Ugh, today was endless. I feel so drained.” I knew she needed someone to listen, to offer comfort, and I wanted to be there for her. But I also felt the pull of my own spiritual needs, the peace I craved from connecting with Allah. My heart tugged in two directions—toward my friend, who counted on me, and toward my faith, which anchored me. I stared at the phone, torn, the weight of both expectations pressing in, unsure which part of myself to answer first.
